subject: Live API degradation during peak — Helix Retail (exec escalation)
messages:
From: Olivia Park <olivia@helixretail.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-27T08:32:00Z
Subject: Live outputs slowing during peak (sample traces attached)

David —

We started seeing elevated token latency and occasional truncated streaming responses starting ~08:22 UTC. The client sees long pauses (10–30s) between token batches for some requests and sporadic 502/524-style gateway errors. This is impacting our live personalization widget during a promotional event.

I attached two things: a short traffic sample (traffic-sample-0327.json) and a list of request IDs we collected (request-ids-helix-0327.txt). Helpful details:
- Peak concurrency hit ~1,200 req/s at 08:20 UTC
- Most affected routes: /v1/live/generate (stream) and /v1/chat/stream
- Latency spikes coincide with bursts from a handful of client IP ranges

Can you confirm this isn’t something on our side? We’re live in 30 minutes for a customer-facing demo, so this is urgent.

Thanks,
Olivia Park
Platform Ops
Helix Retail

---

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia@helixretail.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-27T09:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Live outputs slowing during peak (sample traces attached)

Olivia —

Thanks for the traces and the heads up. We’re prioritizing this and have kicked off a short war room. Immediate asks:
- Can you paste 3 representative request IDs (from the attached file) that show the longest pauses?
- Confirm whether you used the streaming client with automatic reconnects (some clients suppress reconnects which can make symptoms worse).

Initial mitigation steps we’re enacting now:
1) Enable a temporary non-streaming fallback for your high-volume route (switch to polling response model) — this reduces protocol-sensitive chunking pressure.
2) Flip an internal proxy keepalive bump to reduce TCP idle-induced chunk fragmentation (config change, non-disruptive if we throttle properly).
3) Add short-term concurrency cap per-customer to protect shared allocator while we investigate.

Priya & Karthik — I’ve looped you. Priya, can you pull SLO graphs (p50/p95/p99 token latency) and error-rate breakdown across regions for the last 3 hours. Karthik, please surface any autoscaling anomalies and proxy keepalive/idle logs. I’ll coordinate customer comms and exec sync if we need an SLA exception.

Olivia — we’ll try the fallback and get back in 10–15m with a recommendation.

-David
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachments: none in this message

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-27T09:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Live outputs slowing during peak (internal)

Team —

Quick plan (15m ops loop):
- Priya: pull token-level latency and per-route error rate (p50/p95/p99) for 05:00–09:15 UTC and post a short summary. Capture any upticks in cache eviction counters and prefix cache miss rates.
- Karthik: check the serving fleet autoscale history and the proxy layer (lb/proxy) keepalive TTLs, connection churn, and any repeated 5xx patterns. If you see a TTL-induced fragmentation pattern, prepare the config diff to bump keepalive and a safe rollback.
- Evelyn: draft a 1-paragraph exec note summarizing risk & ask (credit decision + SLA exception) so we can go to Marcus if needed.
- David: customer comms & coordinate fallback activation.

We aim to have a short status update at 09:40.

-David

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-27T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Live outputs slowing during peak (technical findings)

Folks —

Prelim findings from the serving and proxy traces:
- Serving runtime observed increased per-token processing jitter for sessions that had a high ratio of short, high-entropy prompts. That increases KV cache churn and causes CPU/GPU scheduling jitter at scale.
- The proxy layer shows a pattern where connections with idle keepalive TTLs are being torn down and then re-established while the client still expects a steady chunk stream — this results in apparent "pauses" from the client POV.
- There are a number of backpressure signals (queue depth spikes) at the proxy edge tied to bursts from a small IP set.

Immediate recommended actions we can apply now:
1) Apply the keepalive bump on the edge proxy (non-disruptive, reduces mid-stream teardown). See attached proxy-config-diff.patch.
2) Temporarily enable per-customer concurrency caps to keep allocator headroom.
3) Advise customer to enable the non-stream fallback for critical demo flows.

I’ll stay on the war room and follow up if I see anything that requires code-level rollback.

-Karthik
Principal Infrastructure Engineer

Attachments: proxy-config-diff.patch (text)

—Olivia

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Olivia Park <olivia@helixretail.com>
Date: 2028-03-27T11:05:00Z
Subject: Escalation: Helix Retail live-stream degradation — exec sync

Marcus/Evelyn —

Summary: Helix Retail (RED-4271) experienced intermittent streaming pauses and elevated token latency during a promotional traffic spike beginning ~08:20 UTC. Symptoms appear to be driven by (1) high client-side burstiness triggering proxy queue spikes and (2) proxy keepalive TTLs tearing mid-stream connections, which amplify client-visible pauses. Karthik’s patch to bump the keepalive and a temporary per-customer concurrency cap have been applied. Customer has enabled a non-streaming fallback for the critical demo.

Impact:
- Customer-visible demo interruptions during a time-sensitive marketing event.
- Error-rate bump from 0.4% → 2.3% for streaming endpoints at peak.
- Elevated p99 token latency (from ~320ms → ~1.8s) on affected routes.

Ask:
- Exec alignment on a goodwill credit: recommend 25% credit for the affected billing window (08:10–09:00 UTC) and a short SLA exception for the live event.
- Approval to include a short-term throttle (per-customer concurrency cap) for Helix while we finish a protection plan.

Next steps we’ll take:
1) Post-mortem doc (link below) with root-cause analysis and mitigation plan including a longer-term fix for prefix cache churn and improved backpressure handling.
2) Engineering will prepare a software mitigation to surface backpressure to clients and improve graceful degradation (ETA 2 weeks).
3) Customer success to offer credits and a follow-up QBR.

Links: https://hubspot.redwood.com/HS-99821 | https://drive.redwood.com/incident/RED-4271-streaming-degradation

I’m standing by if you want a quick sync — we can escalate to legal for contract impacts if needed.

-David
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachments: incident-summary-RED-4271.pdf (generated after war room)
